attempts.summary: Discovered that node1 (VyOS) and node2 (CentOS) each have a second, unconfigured NIC forming the actual private link (node1:eth1 <-> node2:enp8s0), separate from the shared/default network that also includes node3 and node4. Built an Ansible playbook (run from control node node4) that: (1) assigns static IPs on the private link, deploys a minimal Python HTTP app on node2 bound to its private IP:8080 under systemd, and restricts port 8080 via firewalld to only node1's private address; (2) configures VyOS node1 with destination NAT (WAN eth0 tcp/8080 -> 10.10.10.2:8080), source NAT/masquerade for the hairpin return path, and a default-deny forward filter with a narrow explicit allow for that one flow. Verified node3 can reach the app only via node1:8080, while direct access to node2 (on either its shared or private IP) is refused/unreachable. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes with boot-id proof of restart and post-recovery verification, including a final fully idempotent Ansible re-run from node4 after its own restart.
